page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors running at an indicated clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The compute topology provides 32 virtual CPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading active at two threads per core. System memory totals 128.0 GB, sustaining a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU.

Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 33 Gbps. The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store or other external network-attached volumes for persistent data. Accelerators are omitted, with a GPU count of zero. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are also not provided.

With its 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, the hardware configuration targets mid-to-large general-purpose enterprise applications. Cost efficiency stems from dedicated core allocation paired with substantial network throughput, making it suitable for distributed microservices, application backends, container orchestration nodes, and continuous integration runners that rely primarily on network storage architectures.
